messages.content: 我想在聖荷西附近的Walmart買蘋果、米飯和12罐瓶裝水。請顯示產品資訊和庫存情況。

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to buy apples, rice, and 12 cans of bottled water at Walmart near San Jose. They want product info and stock status. We need to call the function walmart_purchase with location "San Jose" or "San Jose, CA" and product_list ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"] and pack_size maybe [12] for bottled water? Actually pack_size array should match product_list length. For apples and rice, no pack size. So we can pass pack_size [null, null, 12] or just omit pack_size for those items. The function signature: loc: string, product_list: string[], pack_size?: number[]. So we can pass pack_size [12] but that would mismatch length. We can pass pack_size [null, null, 12] but type is number[]. So maybe we can pass pack_size [12] and the function will interpret for the last item? But better to pass pack_size [12] and the function will apply to the last item? Not sure. The spec says "Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list." So we need array length equal to product_list. So we need pack_size [null, null, 12] but null is not number. Could use 0 or -1 to indicate not applicable. Let's use 0 for not applicable. So pack_size [0, 0, 12]. That matches length 3. We'll call function.

We need to output product info and stock status. The function will return data. We'll then display.
